lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 51, which makes Shift and Ctrl arrows work in list view with Expandable folders.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request 51, which makes shift and control arrows work in list view with Expandable folders.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You press Up or Down, plain or with Shift, Ctrl or both.
The list view moves the cursor exactly as before, into open folders and past Loading rows.
Then it reads the modifiers: none changes nothing, and Ctrl puts the old selection back.
With Shift, it selects every file from the anchor to the cursor, and never a Loading row.
With Expandable folders on, Thunar handles the arrow keys itself, and that code ignored Shift and Ctrl.
GTK's own keys would stop on Loading rows, so the range is selected one file at a time instead.
Before moving, the key handler notes the cursor, and with Ctrl, the selected rows.
The existing cursor steps run unchanged, which leaves only the new row selected.
With Ctrl, the saved selection comes back, so Ctrl+Space can add the cursor row.
lines.say: With control, the saved selection comes back, so control space can add the cursor row.

lines.caption: The anchor is where the cursor last landed other than by a Shift or Ctrl arrow; with Ctrl, the range is only added.
lines.say: The anchor is where the cursor last landed other than by a shift or control arrow; with control, the range is only added.

lines.caption: Here is what each key does after clicking file1 in a folder of six files.
lines.say: Here is what each key does after clicking file one in a folder of six files.

lines.caption: Shift+Down twice now selects file1 to file3, and Shift+Up shrinks it to two.
lines.say: Shift down twice now selects file one to file three, and shift up shrinks it to two.

lines.caption: Ctrl+Down twice and Ctrl+Space now give file1 and file3.
lines.say: Control down twice and control space now give file one and file three.

lines.caption: Across an open folder, Shift+Down takes the folder and its files.
lines.say: Across an open folder, shift down takes the folder and its files.

lines.caption: Plain keys, and everything with Expandable folders off, are unchanged.
To undo it, revert this PR; nothing is saved anywhere.
The PR changes one source file and adds its test, this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It builds on the existing key handler, GTK's behaviour with the option off, and the copy check from issue 22.
It builds cleanly as Debian packages.
Under Xvfb, Shift extended both ways and after a Ctrl move; Ctrl kept file1, and Shift+Ctrl added to it.
lines.say: Under X V F B, shift extended both ways and after a control move; control kept file one, and shift control added to it.

lines.caption: A right-click kept the anchor, Shift crossed an open folder, plain keys select one row, and the option off changed nothing.
On the latest fix, both sandbox tests passed, and an auditor agent found every screenshot right.
A Loading row was never seen on screen: a small folder loads too fast under Xvfb.
lines.say: A Loading row was never seen on screen: a small folder loads too fast under X V F B.

lines.caption: Each selection is checked by copying it into a folder; CI repeats it and posts its own screenshots.
A fresh review agent found no leaks or crashes, one medium finding and three low ones.
The medium one: an old anchor could come back after plain arrows; the test now checks that.
The status bar now updates once per key press, and the range stops at an anchor hidden in a closed folder.
Kept: Shift with End, Page Down or a click is still GTK's, and starts from the cursor.
lines.say: Kept: shift with end, page down or a click is still G T K's, and starts from the cursor.

lines.caption: CI's own review then found twelve more, three of them medium, and pushed fixes for ten.
The anchor now follows every cursor move but Shift and Ctrl arrows, and the status bar updates once per move.
lines.say: The anchor now follows every cursor move but shift and control arrows, and the status bar updates once per move.

lines.caption: One of its changes was taken back later; the GTK anchor limit stays.
lines.say: One of its changes was taken back later; the G T K anchor limit stays.

lines.caption: The next review found two more medium ones: Ctrl+Space now moves the anchor to the row it toggles.
lines.say: The next review found two more medium ones: control space now moves the anchor to the row it toggles.

lines.caption: And Shift+Ctrl now only adds to the selection, as the issue asks; two older Right key bugs are left for later.
lines.say: And shift control now only adds to the selection, as the issue asks; two older right key bugs are left for later.

lines.caption: A third review found that a right-click on a selected row dropped the anchor again; it is kept now, and tested.
GTK's own Ctrl+Shift arrows only move the cursor; here they add the range, as the issue specifies.
lines.say: G T K's own control shift arrows only move the cursor; here they add the range, as the issue specifies.

lines.caption: After the merge, try it in your own folders, and run the split view crash check.
Part 3. Nothing depends on issue 49, so only your own check remains.
Shift-select across an open folder in a real session, then run the split view check.
lines.say: Shift select across an open folder in a real session, then run the split view check.

lines.caption: In short: Shift and Ctrl arrows now select in list view with Expandable folders, just as everywhere else.
lines.say: In short: shift and control arrows now select in list view with Expandable folders, just as everywhere else.
